newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-YTT sets 17 stg/share teaser for Granada.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-YTT sets 17 stg/share teaser for Granada.

text.p: Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc chairman Ward Thomas said on Tuesday that a takeover bid for his company should be pitched as high as 17 pounds per share.

Neighbouring ITV company Granada Group Plc has built up a total stake of some 27 percent in YTT and has long been expected to mount a takeover bid. That scenario has pushed YTT shares to their current 1250p level, a P/E ratio of over 30.
"I say 17 pounds to Gerry (Granada chairman Gerry Robinson)," Thomas told Reuters in a telephone interview. "It's a conversational gambit," he added.
YTT's 1996 pre-tax profit rose 40 percent to 30.2 million pounds but Thomas said that he believed that a substantial improvement on that level was possible.

He believed that the outlook for the company could be transformed if it wins its battle to cut its annual licence payments from their 1996 level of 66 million pounds and takes its share of ITV advertising back up towards past levels.
Thomas said he did not want to make specific profit forecasts but added it was "not difficult" to visualise YTT making 100 million pounds annually.
Thomas is campaigning for the ITV licence fee system to be replaced by a duty payable by all commercial broadcasters, including BSkyB and Channel 4.

He said that a rate of 16 percent would save YTT as much as 30 million pounds per annum and ensure that the Treasury would still receive the 400 million pounds it currently gets from the ITV companies.
Thomas said support was growing for the plan but added that neither of Britain's main political parties would commit themselves to such a move before the election due by May.
Thomas said that YTT ought to be getting a share of 12-12.5 percent of total ITV advertising revenue, rather than the 10.31 percent it achieved in 1996.
He said his ultimate target was to restore share to the 14 percent level achieved for many years in the past.
YTT said that it was in talks with Laser, its advertising sales house, over marketing the whole of northern England as a single region to boost share. Laser is owned by Granada.
"We need to emphasise the north as a totality," he said.
